subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw support web Mission Control workspace-wide editing and any system filesystem browsing, and what permission boundary should replace or sit beside the current `agents.files.*` allowlist?
rationale: This changes which local files operator clients can read or mutate, overlaps the canonical workspace-management thread, and the system-scope request goes beyond the bounded workspace API already added on main.

options.title: Approve workspace-only path first
options.body: Use the existing read-only `agents.workspace.*` foundation and decide the minimum safe write/upload/delete contract through the canonical workspace-management issue while deferring system filesystem browsing.

options.title: Keep bootstrap editing only
options.body: Leave web Mission Control edits limited to allowlisted bootstrap files and treat broader workspace access as mobile/read-only or future work.

options.title: Open a separate system-scope design
options.body: Track host filesystem browsing separately with explicit opt-in, stronger scopes, auditing, read/write limits, and recovery UX before any code work starts.

recommendation.title: Approve workspace-only path first
recommendation.body: Use the existing read-only `agents.workspace.*` foundation and decide the minimum safe write/upload/delete contract through the canonical workspace-management issue while deferring system filesystem browsing.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the read-only workspace API slice and recent mobile implementation and are the clearest owner for deciding whether to expand that boundary.
